title: fix(agents): record background results at request boundaries
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background task results accepted during an assistant run can appear at a different position when the conversation is reopened, breaking the previously sent prompt prefix. A result arriving during streaming can even move ahead of signed assistant output.

## User Impact

Background completions remain immediately durable and visible. Subsequent model requests preserve their recorded order across live execution and replay, including recovery after an interrupted run. Existing transcripts keep their current interpretation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approved persisted-contract extension records placement with an immutable transcript marker at the next request boundary. It references the original result entries and the exact preceding entry. Live execution adopts those recorded results without importing foreign queued user input, rewriting accepted payloads, or waiting for the parent run to settle.

Bounded and model-context reads, compaction/reset, forks, and suffix cleanup preserve the marker's dependencies. Pending payloads remain recoverable before placement, including through cached reads. There is no database table migration or transcript version bump. Older readers omit newly pending results from model context; the results remain visible in transcript history.

This is one complete persisted-contract cutover: the producer, live loop, replay, and lifecycle consumers must agree before the new marker can be written. Production TypeScript is +789/−69 lines (net +720); tests are +724/−30 (net +694). The growth supports that contract across existing owners, rather than a parallel execution path. No test-line ceiling increase is needed.

## Evidence

Both real-producer timing regressions fail on main `f9135d23491031bbc55bd265f5be07c246b6139b`: tool-time arrival preserves only 4 of 6 prior Responses input items; streaming arrival inserts ahead of signed reasoning. The regression captures the real Responses request builder with synthetic messages, without sending a provider request. Candidate assertions check byte-exact prefix extension, live/replay equality, and unchanged accepted transcript bytes.

- Initial complete consumer run: 119 tests passed across 10 files, including both timing variants, interrupted-run recovery, bounded cleanup, forks/resets, rewrite references, all 14 prompt-prefix tests, and next-turn consumers.
- Final agent-loop, Responses-continuation, and argument-preparation tests: 43 passed. The request-hook tests moved intact into the existing continuation file; the oversized loop delegates its unchanged synchronous argument-preparation block to the existing tool-execution owner. Line-cap ratchet passed without raising caps.
- Existing live-input tests: 7 passed, including foreign-input isolation.
- PR wrapper closure: both previously failing checks now pass after adding the new modules to its inventory; the other 36 tooling checks passed in the earlier run.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root`: all four shards passed.

- Review-fix validation: 47 tests passed across five files, including both original timing variants, all four original recovery modes, cached pending-payload hydration, byte limits, and zero acquisition of unrelated excluded navigation.
- All five interrupted-run recovery modes passed; the final bounded tests also prove that the omitted middle history stays unhydrated.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-file oxlint, and oxfmt checks passed.
- Exact-head CI test-line ratchet passed: 6,299,756 lines against a 6,311,720 ceiling, with 11,964 lines of headroom. The ceiling is unchanged.

- Codex autoreview completed through P2. Both accepted findings were fixed. A final bounded-ancestry concern was rejected: `SessionManager.getEntry()` already returns normalized parents; the added real-producer regression confirms recovery with only the pending result and newest input hydrated across omitted middle history. No accepted findings remain. Two subsequent Codex reviews of the CI repair batch were clean through P2, including the final fixture and assertion-baseline changes. Rebase retained the upstream replay-test repair unchanged; production changes are identical to the reviewed patch. Export-name collision guard passed.

CI found and the follow-up repairs address a bounded-read regression: dependency selection now checks the stored classification before evaluating model navigation, so it does not parse omitted malformed history or legacy duplicate-key rows. The unchanged tests for both cases pass. Marker projection now uses the existing dialect-aware JSON helper; the dialect guard remains at 25 design and 4 mechanical constructs. The moved argument-preparation cast has its validation invariant documented, and its old unused assertion allowance was removed.

The replay-cohort rewrite failures reproduced on unchanged base `6c9614337c050e379a0d01cd469c3fd6db36b001` (both cases failed). They were stale expectations after #187989 introduced a fresh read on the first conflict. The upstream repair in #188398 now requires empty fresh preparation without a replay callback, or rejection of the obsolete final projection, while still proving no stale input is consumed. We kept that upstream test unchanged when rebasing; this PR does not duplicate its repair. All close/revoke cases passed in the equivalent local repair run. The inherited PostgreSQL backup/config alias failure is resolved by rebasing over the upstream fix `34a4e118dc1d`, without copying it into this branch.

The repair run passed 148 tests across seven files. The final fixture check, targeted source-test typechecks, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and all four `pnpm tsgo:test:root` shards passed. Changed-file oxlint and oxfmt passed. No runtime performance improvement is claimed. Exact-head CI passed at `f606d930c269a187dbd51e851fe731803d564213` ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41075553980)), including all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs. The PR is ready and intentionally unmerged.
